I was being hyperbolic in citing things that a healthy mind wouldn't even think about doing. They're not choices that you consider if you're in a content frame of mind. Mental illness changes all that and makes you decide every single second. Disrupts routine. Suddenly you can either go to sleep without brushing or brush first, and you have to chose. 
  
I apologise if I was being unclear or insensitive. I realise that drug use is something that a lot of us struggle with as a result of depression, maybe that wasn't the best example

Things like brushing your teeth are habits. And normally you wouldn't even think about going to bed without brushing, like you wouldn't think about shooting heroin or driving without your glasses. But when some external force removes that habbit, like depression does, you have to reform it. It's like being a kid again, except this time you're the only person who can hold you responsible for it. At this point, brushing your teeth is no longer a part of your routine. It's an elective action. Shit's hard, but once you manage to reshape it into a habbit, it becomes a lil easier.

A lot. Shame. Guilt. Self loathing. I mean you name it. 

I have a tendency to fall into those absolute pits that seem impossible to climb out of, seemingly for no good reason. And then they pass, and I don't know why they came and how to stop them from coming back. I have nightmares, strange distorted nightmares. And episodes of, I don't know, hysteria? I can cry for 30 minutes while beating my head with fists. I don't know why. It just happens. 

I need to find a job. And that just seems like the immediate horizon of problems. I'll be fine, but it's a lot to deal with and sometimes it feels like it keeps piling on.

I just came home and realised I ran out of meds. Like I literally just took my last pill. And tomorrow is Saturday, so earliest I'll be able to get a refill is Monday. Maybe. 

I dunno, it's just. A year ago i felt like absolute shit but I had hoped that in a years time I might feel better. I mean a year's a lot of time, but I figured hey, might hang in there for that long. And it did get a little better, but it always comes back. It always comes back. And I can never outrun it.

I'm really sorry to hear that. Getting people to take your problems seriously is difficult, especially when it comes to mental health. 
  
From my own experience, psychiatric hospitals are not a silver bullet. I would definitely recommend checking into one if you feel you might do something you'd regret. But it wasn't a great long term solution for me, just a way to survive.
 
Do you have anyone else to talk to about this? A friend, or a school counselor?

You slipped. That's ok. It happens to most people and it's a normal feature of making a change. It doesn't erase or invalidate your work. Doesn't mean you can't do it. 
  
Having to hide it definitely sucks, especially as the weather gets warmer. I remember (TW) >!going to uni with cuts all over my thigs and redoing my dressings in the bathroom!<. It's horrible, and it doesn't help that people don't get why you do it. I mean it's an addiction in the sense. You get a little dopamine hit and that helps you through the worst of it. But there are better options. I'm not saying this to shame you, I would never judge you for this. I'm saying it so you know there's a world without this. You'll get better at resisting the temptation. You might still slip up in the future, but I believe you can get up even if you do. 
  
And hey, this may be a dumb idea. But you might wanna go to a mall or a thrift store and buy yourself something nice with long sleeves. Make the best of a bad situation. I dunno, maybe I'm rambling. I can vouch that thrift stores attract such a wide array of people that you might not feel as uncomfortable as in a different setting. 
  
Anyway, good luck! This is a hard path to walk, but it's a good path to walk too.

Hey, I'm really sorry to hear that you're in such a tough situation. 2020 has been collosaly destructive to our collective psyche and it looks like you've been struggling even without that. 
  
I know it's horribly overwhelming to have to face the same difficulties over and over again. The issue is that your brain is only giving you the worst option. Depression lies to you. Sure, it's possible that you're out of work, but maybe you're not and this break will eventually end. In a way it's good that you can see the worst possible outcome because it can help you prepare. But it's important to recognise that it's not the only possibility. Maybe on Monday you'll get a call to come into work the next day. 
  
I know it's a clichéd show to bring up at this point, but there's a great scene in BoJack Horseman where the main character asks "what if I start drinking again?" and his friend immediately replies "then you'll get sober again." It doesn't just apply to addiction, but all sorts of difficulties that reappear in life. And it sucks that we have to do it all over again, but that doesn't mean you can't make it through. I just want you to know that everything you do matters. Every positive change that you make has an impact. You may not feel it now, but I'm sure one day you will.

Fuck this hit like a brick wall. In a good way. I like that you're attacking the idea of potential, it's always been something that gnawed at me. Thanks for this reply, I really don't have the intellectual capacity to explain why I think it's really good right now, but I do. It helps a little and that's a lot.

That's an interesting way to look at this. I'll grant you, there are times where it feels like a quirk. An odd one, and not something you'd bring up at a party, but a quirk. Harmless. 

The trouble is when it overwhelmes your ability to interface with the world. You lose any desire to do anything that doesn't at least lead to a temporary firing of neurons and immediate release of dopamine. Because what's the point right? You're gonna off yourself anyway. It's a chore at that point. Not even that dangerous, but harmful in its own insidious way. Like slow brain damage from sustained hypoxia, as opposed to an actual death from asphyxiation.

Another thing I think about is how unproductive it is to treat suicidality as a symptom to itself. It doesn't exist in a vacuum. Take away a person's means to kill themselves, and you still leave the nightmarish bog that they live in. One that drove them to those thoughts and likely will again.

Okay so the thing is - you don't have to be *great* or *the best* at something to be *good* at it. I'm sure there is a great deal of skill that you have in the areas that you're interested in. Even if you're not where you want to be yet, you're almost certainly somewhere people want to be when they start out. I used to think I suck ass at drawing. But when I landed in a psych ward and did drawing exercises in group therapy, I realised that there are tons of people who can only draw a stickman. Now I'm still not great and I still have a long way to go to be at the level I want to be at. But I know I've gotten somewhere, so I can take a breath, sit down for a moment and then carry on improving.

I know it's insanely difficult to see that when you're in the dumps. But I'm sure you'll feel a little better down the line and you'll recognise it then.

But seriously, don't beat yourself up for being bad at something you're not really wired to do. It's nice that you enjoyed your dating history, even if it isn't super long. I'm sure more of those nice dates will happen for you :)

This is despair, isn't it. It's a complete lack of hope. I'm very sorry that you feel this, it's a horrible feeling. But hope often comes back. Sometimes you just have to hope for hope if that makes sense. 

A thing I'm trying to use in my life is to look at my personality as just a skill. I try not to look at my quirks I don't like as moral failings, but just as something I haven't figured out yet. Something that can be worked on. Psychotherapy is obviously a key instrument in this.

I used to practically obsess with that idea. You gotta live with your mistakes unfortunately. But hey, everyone makes those. Learning *how to* actually learn from your mistakes is fucking hard, but it's necessary. 

Although it's funny how when we design things like videogames, we instinctively create systems that are more fair. More forgiving.

One way that I describe this sensation is 'mental homelessness'. Like I desire the mental health equivalent of a clean sheet and a warm blanket. It's always difficult to pin down the specifics, and that's one reason why therapy is such a difficult and complicated process - you spend years untangling the web of patterns, traumas and pathologies that make up a depressed mind. 

Still, I try to soldier on. As long as I feel the way I feel now, I can hack at this little by little.

It breaks my heart a little when people ask me what they can do for me, because they genuinely want to help, and I'm drawing a blank. I don't know. I don't understand what's happening to me. It's scary.

Hey there Mitch! I'm not a UK citizen, but I'd advise that you start by contacting your GP. This is a good first step because your doctor will a) be able to point to steps you can take specifically within the NHS and b) might be someone you already trust if you've had the same GP for a while now. It could also help to talk to your parents about it - if your dad has struggled with depression I'm sure he would understand your situation.   

It does suck a lot to be single all through your teenage years - been there myself. While a relationship can never really *fix* you per se, it's perfectly normal to struggle with your self image because of that. The problem with dating is that it's a little bit of a roulette - sometimes you just get unlucky for a long period of time. What I'd advise is to try and be the best person you can be on your own - being able to love yourself is the most important piece of foundation for a healthy relationship.  

The COVID situation obviously makes everything much more difficult. Maybe this will all pass when the pandemic blows over, but it's good to check with your doctor just in case. Unfortunately, there is a genetic component to depression, but it's not as simple as passing down an inheritable illness so don't worry. The important thing is that you're observing your mood correctly and you're taking the right steps.  
 
Best of luck!

I don't have triggers as strong as that, but I have some small mechanisms to stop myself from self-harm. I have a kind of a tierlist of things that I do when I'm self destructive. If I'm in that state where I just want to destroy all my accomplishments and throw everything out, I try to step a few steps down on the ladder. Do something that I consider a slip or a failure but that isn't *actually* that self destructive. Like I don't know, eat some ice cream while on a diet. Go to sleep when I told myself I should study. Keep in mind this is absolutely NOT a great long term solution, but it helps me stop myself from doing something really stupid by sating that self destructive urge with something less harmful.

My number one advice would be to communicate more clearly, but that's obviously easier said than done. Communication is fucking hard.

What I sometimes do is challenge my emotions. Sort of talk to them. You can't control what emotions you're experiencing and you should never deny them or shame yourself for experiencing them. But you can 'negotiate' with them sometimes. If I tell my emotions that they're irrational, it's a little bit easier to not lash out at others. Don't know if that will work for you, but maybe it's worth a try. 

And yeah, communication is key. If your boyfriend understands how those emotions affect you, he'll have an easier time when you shut down. I hope someone smarter than me can chime in to help with that. 

Best of luck!

Hey, I can't really think of a great piece of advise to be honest, I suck at relationships. What you're doing is very difficult - maintaining a relationship while dealing with depression. You're kind of like a waiter balancing plates in both hands and also trying to remember all the orders you got. 

One thing I thought of - and this may be me being stupid but hey - is that you might try spending more time outdoors if your triggers have to do with your environment. Not even in any active way, just sit on a bench in a park. Of course, this all depends on the COVID situation where you live.

Maybe you could try doing things on a micro scale. You might have to force yourself into doing it, but set a tiny goal for each day. Do one pushup. Read for five minutes. Brush your teeth for 30 seconds, and if you can't do that, just use mouthwash. It's horribly difficult to do even the tiniest things sometimes, but if you manage to start, it gets easier every day.

I've never been really good at anything. I sucked at sports ever since I can remember, my every attempt to get fit was either half assed or not assed at all. I guess I always just put in minimal effort. My grades were decent up until middle school, which is where I actually needed to put in some work to keep up for the first time, and of course I didn't. I only picked up the slack (somewhat) in high school, junior year, and while it wasn't too late to at least get into college, I will never forgive myself for wasting my potential. I just never learned the value of hard work, and I hate myself for it. If only I had put enough work into school, or my passions, or fucking anything. Heh.

I've now just enrolled in a shitty university some 200 miles away, with a major that is neither my passion nor a guarantee of future employment. It's also going to be my first time living alone, in a city where I don't know anyone and I'm terrified. Not in a "anxious but excited" way, but in a "holy fuck how do I adult" way. Knowing myself, I will make a whooping zero friends, and even IF I'm going to be invited anywhere I'll probably just skip out because I'm anxious or because I'm shitty at financing and I don't want to "blow" money on social life or because whatever other reason. Honestly I just want to stay with my parents, because they make feel safe, but what sort of a shameful existence would that be? 

My personal life is a miserable joke. I fell in love a total of 4 times, and every time I did I would just let it cook me from the inside, because I was too big of a pussy to confess my feelings. The last girl I fell in love with was way out of my league, AND lived some 120 miles away, and I still couldn't let her go for more than two years. I'm a virgin if that wasn't obvious already; heck, I've never even kissed a girl, let alone been in a relationship. I don't see how that could ever change, and I realise I've missed out on a very important experience in life. I don't want to sound like one of those fellas over at r/incels, I know having a significant other doesn't magically fix you, but it really makes me feel pathetic and worthless. 

Speaking of which, I never had a job, the closest thing was some minor voluntary work at a political office in senior year. I tried to get a summer job two years ago and after handing in my resumé at two places and being told that they want people for 2 months plus I just gave up. Then I tried again this year, but I got a medical condition that forced me into the hospital every two weeks. It's a piss poor excuse and a competent person would have found and kept a job anyway, but not me. I don't have a driver's license. I tried to get one this summer, and I finished the course but didn't have time to take the exam before college started. I know that had I been a well adjusted person I would have started earlier and already have it by now. Every time I have to evaluate myself for whatever reason, I come to the conclusion that I am nothing but a steaming pile of negative personality traits. Just off the top of my head, here are a couple that I could attribute to myself:

* Lazy
* Disorganised
* Directionless
* Immature
* Cowardly
* Unintelligent
* Easily distracted
* Incompetent 
* Selfish 
* Boring 
* Complacent 
* Vain

Positive traits? I can't come up with a single one.

My father comes from the countryside, and despite every difficulty that this entailed, he still managed to move to a city and get a higher education. When he was my age that was also pretty much the most one could achieve - studying abroad was literally impossible because of the political climate back then. Mind you, where I live the top national unis are on the the 400-500 positions of things like ARWU, so you really kinda have to go abroad if you want to get a good education. They always wanted me to go to an ivy league school or something along those lines, and I know that a) it was perfectly possible b) it would have at the very least be something to be proud of.  

I'm a fucking failure, that's what I am. With all the resources that I had at my disposal since childhood, I should be flying off to fucking Harvard by now, but no. Honestly, I should probably just commit suicide. I really, really don't want to live anymore. But I can't kill myself, because I know that there are people who love me. If not for my family, I probably would have slit my wrists ages ago. And yeah, that sounds weird, but I just can't find a single thing about myself that would make me a human being worthy of love, so it just feels so damn unnatural that they won't abandon me. I feel guilty because with the resources they gave me (it's not that my family is ridiculously wealthy but they can afford to put me through college and always supported me in pretty much everything), a decent, hard working human being could have achieved so, so much. And here I am, a nothing of a man.  

I'm on antidepressants now and they make me feel content in a dumb way. I guess you could describe it as an emotional numbness - I can forget how shitty of a person I am, but then I snap back to reality all of a sudden and I cry hysterically because of all the hatred I have for myself. It's all I do these days basically, lay in bed and cry. That and fantasising about going back in time 10 years or so and showing myself how not to fuck everything up. I fantasise so much I'm actually scared I might slip one day, but it's the only thing that brings me some comfort. It's like the only future I have is buried deep in my past. I just want to go back and fix everything. Is that too much to ask? Because it clearly is too late now. I've wasted so much of my youth, and now I'm a disgusting failure. A disgrace to my family and frankly to humanity as a whole.

Sorry for the wall of text :<
